job.style: a comparison of two related ideas

passage: Water scarcity is a complex issue that extends far beyond simple rainfall patterns, as it is frequently driven by the over-exploitation and unequal distribution of water across different social groups. While many believe that dams are the ultimate cure for floods, they often fail to achieve this because large reservoirs can actually trigger floods during heavy downpours when excess water must be released suddenly. Furthermore, water management is not a task limited to the countryside; urban centers face severe shortages that require modern, integrated rainwater harvesting systems to supplement their supply. Traditional methods of water conservation, once dismissed as primitive, are now being revived in cities to combat the growing crisis caused by industrial pollution and inefficient usage. By shifting our focus from large-scale engineering projects to community-led conservation, we can address the root causes of water stress. Effective management requires acknowledging that scarcity is a human-made problem, often resulting from poor planning and the mismanagement of resources rather than just a lack of precipitation. Sustainable development depends on integrating these traditional wisdoms with modern technology to ensure that every household, whether in a bustling metropolis or a remote village, has access to clean and reliable water throughout the year.

items.evidence: While many believe that dams are the ultimate cure for floods, they often fail to achieve this because large reservoirs can actually trigger floods during heavy downpours when excess water must be released suddenly.
items.q: Why can a dam fail to stop floods during very heavy rain?
options: Extra water has to be let out suddenly
Dams are built only to produce electricity
Reservoirs hold rainwater but never release it
Dams cannot store any water in monsoon
items.explain: In heavy rain a full reservoir must release excess water suddenly, and that release can itself cause floods.

wrong.why: thinks dams exist only for electricity, not flood control
reverses the cause: thinks the reservoir never releases water
assumes dams always work, so blames the rain itself

items.evidence: Furthermore, water management is not a task limited to the countryside; urban centers face severe shortages that require modern, integrated rainwater harvesting systems to supplement their supply.
items.q: A big city's taps run short every summer. What should it do, by this passage?
options: Collect rainwater to add to its supply
Leave harvesting to villages with farms
Blame low rainfall and wait for monsoon
Rely only on building bigger dams
items.explain: Cities face severe shortages and need rainwater harvesting systems to supplement supply; it is not only for villages.

wrong.why: thinks rainwater harvesting is only for rural areas
thinks scarcity comes only from lack of rain
thinks big dams are always the best fix

items.evidence: Effective management requires acknowledging that scarcity is a human-made problem, often resulting from poor planning and the mismanagement of resources rather than just a lack of precipitation.
items.q: A region gets good rain, yet its people face water shortage. Which explains this best?
options: Poor planning and misuse of its water
Rainfall alone decides how much water exists
A growing population needs only more food
Dirty water still counts as available water
items.explain: Scarcity is human-made, often from poor planning and mismanagement, not just lack of rain.

wrong.why: thinks scarcity is caused only by lack of rainfall
thinks population growth affects only food, not water
thinks polluted water is still usable supply

items.evidence: Traditional methods of water conservation, once dismissed as primitive, are now being revived in cities to combat the growing crisis caused by industrial pollution and inefficient usage.
items.q: Why are cities now reviving traditional water conservation methods?
options: To fight a crisis of pollution and waste
To replace modern technology completely
To show that dams are the best answer
To stop rain from falling on cities
items.explain: Cities are reviving old methods to combat a growing crisis caused by pollution and inefficient water use.

wrong.why: ignores that the passage wants old and modern methods combined
thinks dams are always the best solution
blames only rainfall for the city's problem

items.evidence: By shifting our focus from large-scale engineering projects to community-led conservation, we can address the root causes of water stress.
items.q: Why does the passage favour community-led conservation over only building huge engineering projects?
options: It tackles the root causes of water stress
It stops every flood in the country
It produces more electricity than any dam
It proves that big projects harm every river
items.explain: Community-led conservation addresses the root causes of water stress, which large projects alone do not.

wrong.why: thinks flood control is the main aim of water projects
thinks water projects are mainly for electricity
over-generalises about dams, swinging from only benefits to only harm
